subject: Copywriting
title: The CAN-SPAM Act
description: A fast breakdown of The CAN-SPAM Act for builders.

hook.text: By 2003, spam was 45% of all email. Congress passed the CAN-SPAM Act. For the first time, email marketing had rules.

buildup.text: CAN-SPAM required honest subject lines, a physical address, and a working unsubscribe link in every commercial email.

discovery.text: Legitimate marketers welcomed it. Rules separated them from spammers and increased consumer trust in email.

twist.text: Penalties reached $46,517 per violation. But enforcement was weak and spam continued to grow despite the law.

climax.text: GDPR in 2018 went further: explicit consent required before sending. Email marketing shifted from opt-out to opt-in.

punchline.text: Consent became mandatory. Permission email is the only email now.

quiz.question: What did the CAN-SPAM Act require in every email?

details.summary: The CAN-SPAM Act of 2003 established rules for commercial email in the United States, requiring honest subject lines, clear sender identification, a physical address, and a working unsubscribe mechanism. Violations can result in penalties of up to $46,517 per email sent.
details.whyItMatters: CAN-SPAM set the legal framework for email marketing in the US. Understanding compliance is essential for any business sending commercial emails — violations carry severe financial penalties.
takeaways: Every commercial email must include a working unsubscribe mechanism
Subject lines must not be deceptive about the email's content
Penalties can reach $46,517 per individual violating email

faq.question: What are the main requirements of the CAN-SPAM Act?
faq.answer: Don't use false header information. Don't use deceptive subject lines. Identify the message as an ad. Include your physical postal address. Tell recipients how to opt out. Honor opt-outs within 10 business days. Monitor what others do on your behalf.

faq.question: Does CAN-SPAM require opt-in consent?
faq.answer: No — unlike GDPR in Europe, CAN-SPAM does not require prior consent to send commercial email. It is an opt-out system: you can email anyone until they unsubscribe. However, best practices and higher conversion rates both favor opt-in lists.
